primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency impairs conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine, causing phenylalanine accumulation and reduced tyrosine availability.
vignette: Newborn screening shows markedly elevated phenylalanine. Molecular testing identifies biallelic PAH variants.
lead: Which biochemical reaction is most directly impaired?
distractor_notes: Tyrosine conversion toward catecholamines occurs downstream and is not the primary PAH defect.
Homocysteine to cystathionine is catalyzed by cystathionine beta-synthase.
Galactose-1-phosphate metabolism is impaired in classic galactosemia.
Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid oxidation is impaired in maple syrup urine disease.
key_expl: PAH encodes phenylalanine hydroxylase, which converts phenylalanine to tyrosine.
objective: Identify the blocked biochemical reaction in classic phenylketonuria.

sources.title: Phenylketonuria
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes PKU as impaired phenylalanine breakdown, most commonly from PAH deficiency.

sources.title: PAH gene
sources.support: PAH encodes phenylalanine hydroxylase, which converts phenylalanine to tyrosine.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: GALT deficiency blocks conversion of galactose-1-phosphate with UDP-glucose, causing toxic galactose-1-phosphate accumulation after lactose-containing feeds.
vignette: A 9-day-old infant develops vomiting, jaundice, hepatomegaly, and poor feeding after milk feeds are established. Galactose-1-phosphate is elevated.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: Galactokinase deficiency causes a milder disorder dominated by cataracts rather than classic systemic galactosemia.
Fructokinase deficiency causes benign essential fructosuria.
Aldolase B deficiency causes hereditary fructose intolerance.
Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type I.
key_expl: Classic galactosemia is caused by severe deficiency of GALT, leading to galactose-1-phosphate accumulation.
objective: Identify GALT deficiency in a neonate who becomes ill after lactose exposure.

sources.title: Galactosemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes classic galactosemia as GALT deficiency causing toxic galactose metabolites after milk exposure.

sources.title: GALT gene
sources.support: GALT encodes galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase, a key enzyme in galactose metabolism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Deficiency of branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase prevents oxidative decarboxylation of leucine, isoleucine, and valine metabolites, causing neurotoxic accumulation.
vignette: A 6-day-old newborn has poor feeding, lethargy, intermittent opisthotonos, and urine with a sweet odor. Leucine, isoleucine, and valine are elevated.
distractor_notes: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU.
Homogentisate dioxygenase deficiency causes alkaptonuria.
Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency causes classic homocystinuria.
Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency causes propionic acidemia, a different organic acidemia.
key_expl: MSUD results from deficient branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase activity.
objective: Relate neonatal encephalopathy with sweet-smelling urine to failure of branched-chain amino acid catabolism.

sources.title: Maple syrup urine disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes MSUD as impaired breakdown of branched-chain amino acids due to deficient branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex.

sources.title: BCKDHA gene
sources.support: BCKDHA encodes a component of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes neuronal GM2 ganglioside accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration without the hepatosplenomegaly typical of several other lysosomal storage disorders.
vignette: A 7-month-old infant has loss of motor milestones, exaggerated startle response, hypotonia, and a cherry-red macular spot. There is no hepatosplenomegaly.
distractor_notes: Niemann-Pick type A can cause a cherry-red spot but usually includes prominent hepatosplenomegaly from sphingomyelin storage.
Gaucher disease causes hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone disease rather than this classic infantile neurodegenerative pattern.
Pompe disease causes hypotonia and cardiomyopathy from lysosomal glycogen accumulation, not a cherry-red macula.
Krabbe disease causes severe demyelinating neurodegeneration but not the classic GM2/cherry-red-without-visceromegaly pattern.
key_expl: Infantile neurodegeneration with exaggerated startle, cherry-red macula, and absent hepatosplenomegaly is classic Tay-Sachs disease.
objective: Differentiate Tay-Sachs from other lysosomal storage disorders using neurologic and visceral findings.

sources.title: Tay-Sachs disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Tay-Sachs as HEXA-related GM2 accumulation causing progressive neurologic deterioration and a cherry-red spot.

sources.title: HEXA gene
sources.support: HEXA encodes a subunit of beta-hexosaminidase A, which is required for GM2 ganglioside degradation.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes glucocerebroside accumulation within macrophage lysosomes, producing hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone disease.
vignette: A 14-year-old child has massive splenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and recurrent bone pain. Bone marrow shows lipid-laden macrophages with fibrillary cytoplasm.
distractor_notes: Tay-Sachs causes severe neurodegeneration without prominent hepatosplenomegaly.
Niemann-Pick type A causes sphingomyelin accumulation and severe infantile neurologic disease, not the classic bone crises of Gaucher disease.
Fabry disease is X-linked and causes neuropathic pain, angiokeratomas, renal and cardiac disease.
Metachromatic leukodystrophy primarily causes progressive demyelination from sulfatide accumulation.
key_expl: Hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, bone pain, and characteristic lipid-laden macrophages are classic for Gaucher disease.
objective: Recognize Gaucher disease from macrophage lipid storage with visceral and skeletal involvement.

sources.title: Gaucher disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Gaucher disease as GBA-related glucocerebroside accumulation causing enlarged liver and spleen, blood abnormalities, and bone disease.

sources.title: GBA1 gene
sources.support: GBA1 encodes lysosomal glucocerebrosidase, which degrades glucocerebroside.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes lysosomal globotriaosylceramide accumulation in vascular endothelium and multiple organs, producing neuropathic pain, angiokeratomas, renal disease, and cardiomyopathy.
vignette: A 17-year-old boy has recurrent burning pain in his hands and feet, decreased sweating, angiokeratomas, and corneal verticillata. Maternal male relatives have kidney disease.
lead: Which substance accumulates in this disorder?
distractor_notes: GM2 accumulates in Tay-Sachs disease.
Sphingomyelin accumulates in acid sphingomyelinase deficiency.
Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease.
Lysosomal glycogen accumulates in Pompe disease.
key_expl: Fabry disease is caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency and accumulation of globotriaosylceramide.
objective: Identify the stored substrate in X-linked Fabry disease.
clues: X-linked family pattern with renal disease

sources.title: Fabry disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Fabry disease as GLA-related alpha-galactosidase A deficiency with glycosphingolipid accumulation.

sources.title: GLA gene
sources.support: GLA encodes alpha-galactosidase A, which degrades globotriaosylceramide.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ABCD1 deficiency impairs transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes for beta-oxidation, causing VLCFA accumulation and injury to cerebral myelin and adrenal cortex.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy develops behavioral changes, declining school performance, gait abnormalities, and adrenal insufficiency. Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids are markedly elevated.
lead: Which cellular process is primarily impaired?
correct: Transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes
distractors: Transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria by carnitine
Mitochondrial oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids
distractor_notes: Carnitine-dependent mitochondrial entry involves long-chain fatty acids and causes a different class of fatty-acid oxidation disorders.
Sphingomyelin degradation failure causes Niemann-Pick types A/B.
Medium-chain fatty-acid oxidation is impaired in MCAD deficiency.
Cholesterol synthesis is not the primary ABCD1 defect.
key_expl: ABCD1 encodes a peroxisomal transporter required for very-long-chain fatty-acid handling.
objective: Connect elevated very-long-chain fatty acids in X-ALD with defective peroxisomal transport and oxidation.

sources.title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes X-ALD as ABCD1-related VLCFA accumulation affecting nervous system and adrenal glands.

sources.title: ABCD1 gene
sources.support: ABCD1 encodes a peroxisomal membrane transporter involved in very-long-chain fatty-acid import for degradation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pathogenic mitochondrial DNA variants are typically maternally inherited because the embryo's mitochondria derive predominantly from the oocyte; heteroplasmy contributes to variable expression among relatives.
vignette: A woman with a mitochondrial DNA disorder has three children. Her affected brother also has the disorder.
lead: Which transmission pattern is most consistent with mitochondrial DNA inheritance?
correct: An affected mother can transmit the variant to sons and daughters, whereas an affected father does not transmit it
distractors: Only affected fathers transmit the variant to sons
Affected fathers transmit the variant to all daughters
Carrier mothers transmit the variant only to sons
Transmission occurs strictly in a 50% autosomal dominant pattern
distractor_notes: Paternal mitochondrial DNA is generally not the source of offspring mitochondria, so father-to-son transmission is not expected.
Father-to-all-daughters is the pattern of X-linked dominant transmission, not mitochondrial inheritance.
Mitochondrial variants can be transmitted by mothers to offspring of either sex.
Heteroplasmy and mitochondrial segregation make expression more variable than a simple autosomal dominant 50% pattern.
key_expl: Mitochondrial DNA is maternally inherited; affected mothers may transmit variants to children of either sex, whereas affected fathers generally do not transmit mtDNA.
objective: Recognize maternal inheritance as the defining transmission pattern of mitochondrial DNA variants.

sources.title: Mitochondrial inheritance
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics explains that mitochondrial DNA is inherited from the mother and can be passed to sons and daughters.

sources.title: Mitochondrial DNA
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes mitochondrial DNA and its maternal inheritance pattern.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Germline TP53 loss compromises p53-mediated DNA-damage checkpoints, apoptosis, and senescence, allowing genetically damaged cells to survive and predisposing to diverse early cancers.
vignette: A 29-year-old woman with breast cancer has relatives with childhood sarcoma, brain tumor, leukemia, and early adrenal cancer across several generations.
lead: Which cellular function is most directly impaired?
correct: p53-mediated tumor suppression after DNA damage
distractor_notes: MLH1 mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome.
Neurofibromin loss causes NF1 through increased RAS signaling.
APC loss causes familial adenomatous polyposis through increased Wnt/beta-catenin signaling.
ATP7B defects cause Wilson disease, not inherited cancer predisposition.
key_expl: Li-Fraumeni syndrome is caused by germline TP53 pathogenic variants that impair p53 tumor-suppressor responses to cellular stress and DNA damage.
objective: Connect a broad spectrum of very early cancers with germline TP53 loss in Li-Fraumeni syndrome.
clues: sarcoma plus breast and brain tumors

sources.title: Li-Fraumeni syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Li-Fraumeni syndrome as a TP53-related inherited predisposition to many early-onset cancers.

sources.title: TP53 gene
sources.support: TP53 encodes p53, a tumor suppressor that responds to DNA damage by controlling cell-cycle arrest, repair, senescence, and apoptosis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defective nucleotide excision repair prevents removal of bulky ultraviolet-induced DNA lesions such as pyrimidine dimers, causing extreme photosensitivity and early skin cancers.
vignette: A 5-year-old child has severe photosensitivity, extensive freckling on sun-exposed skin, and an early basal cell carcinoma.
lead: Which DNA-repair pathway is most commonly defective?
distractors: Repair of DNA interstrand cross-links by the Fanconi pathway
Base excision repair of uracil only
distractor_notes: Mismatch repair corrects replication-associated base mismatches and is defective in Lynch syndrome.
Homologous recombination repairs double-strand breaks and is not the primary UV-damage pathway in XP.
Fanconi pathway defects cause Fanconi anemia with cross-link sensitivity and marrow failure.
Base excision repair handles small non-helix-distorting lesions; XP classically involves inability to repair bulky UV photoproducts by nucleotide excision repair.
key_expl: Most xeroderma pigmentosum forms result from defective nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA lesions.
objective: Relate severe UV sensitivity and early skin cancer to defective nucleotide excision repair.

sources.title: Xeroderma pigmentosum
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes XP as defective repair of ultraviolet-induced DNA damage with severe photosensitivity and high skin-cancer risk.

sources.title: XPA gene
sources.support: XPA encodes a protein required for nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA lesions.
